name: redirection
notes: Adapter-authoring exercise 2026-08-27: Redirection was selected from the unsupported-candidate ledger after its official WordPress.org listing reported more than two million active installations. The exact official 5.9.0 artifact SHA-256 is b6dd341a6b383440cbb1d5647fa59a82fc5e48afe2165539284c56edaf066842; official 5.8.1 SHA-256 6256d0829120a6661da5e6698cab5f3ead6a830c6d67e4a89a064649fb59ef79 is the below-range refusal control, not inferred support.

The supported profile is single-site Redirection 5.9.0 using only WordPress module id 1. Apache and Nginx groups generate target server files and are refused by the provider before effects; the adapter does not carry modules/location, REST routing, IP proxy/header trust, canonical-domain aliases, relocation, plugin token, database migration markers, update notices, or UI selection history.

redirection_groups and redirection_items both use mapped identity because neither schema has a stable unique natural key. Group names can legally duplicate; item sources can legally duplicate and ordering decides the winner. redirection_items.group_id is rewritten through the same red_group ledger. The activation-created default groups therefore require the ordinary explicit tables adoption authority on a fresh target instead of an unsafe name guess.

redirection_items.action_data is a measured tagged union, not a serialized column: plain target URL string, canonical PHP-serialized matcher map, or SQL NULL depending on the native matcher/action. php_serialized_or_text is feature-gated so an older engine refuses the adapter rather than treating arbitrary bytes as serialization or changing php_serialized/v1 semantics.

redirection_logs and redirection_404 are request history. redirection_items.last_count and last_access are mutable hit telemetry. They stay target-local and are excluded from capture. Deletion is deliberately unsupported: item URLs can be operationally referenced outside WordPress and group deletion cascades through items without a complete reverse-reference grammar.

The provider restricts every group to WordPress_Module::MODULE_ID, calls the plugin's public module flush boundary, rotates Redirection's own cache_key when caching is enabled, resets its in-process cache, and proves database/API/lookup convergence for every row. Its receipt contains counts, hashes, cache-enabled state, and the generation number only; it carries no redirect URLs, matcher payloads, tokens, IP addresses, or request logs.

Only the exact official 5.9.0 release was exercised end to end, so the version interval is [5.9.0, 5.9.1). No compatibility is inferred from the neighboring 5.8.1 artifact or from matching table names.
